title: POC scoping - Cost modeling with Sierra Micro
summary: Discovery / POC scoping focused on per-token cost modeling and performance knobs. Customer wants a 4-week POC with 100k queries/day target, latency SLO 150-300ms p50/p95, and a hard budget cap. Discussed hosted vs dedicated, batching, KV cache, quantization, and security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: send detailed cost model spreadsheet, schedule infra benchmark, and share security pack.
action_items: Alex: Share cost model spreadsheet + sample unit economics by 2026-12-03
Priya: Prepare benchmark plan + test harness and identify sample prompts by 2026-12-04
James: Provide representative traffic profile (qps distribution, avg tokens per request) by 2026-12-03
Lina: Confirm acceptance criteria and which success metrics (latency percentiles, quality thresholds) by 2026-12-05
next_steps: Redwood to run a 2-hour hosted benchmark with Sierra Micro sample prompts (week of 12/7)
Customer to review cost spreadsheet and pick preferred scenario (hosted vs dedicated)
Schedule follow-up to review benchmark results and finalize POC scope (target 12/10-12/12)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood); James Ortega, Lina Park, Evan Ross (Sierra Micro)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. quick round of intros?
[00:08] James: James Ortega, CTO at Sierra Micro. we run the inference stack and lead ML infra.
[00:12] Lina: Lina Park, leading ML team, responsible for model quality and evals.
[00:15] Evan: Evan Ross, infra, I manage our GPU fleet and networking.
[00:19] Alex: Great, I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, and Priya is our SE, she'll lead the technical scoping.
[00:24] Priya: hi all, nice to meet you. quick agenda: understand success criteria, traffic shape, target throughput and latency, then walk through cost levers and POC plan.

[02:03] James: high level, we want to POC to validate unit economics. target is about 100k queries/day initially, with burst to 300 qps during peak. avg prompt size is ~120 tokens input and 80 tokens output.
[02:22] Priya: ok so avg total tokens per request ~200. any batching today?
[02:28] James: not really. we have a simple queuing layer, but no effective batching at app layer.

[04:10] Priya: for cost modeling we usually break down per-token compute cost, and then surface knobs: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization, and routing to cheaper model variants for non-critical traffic. With your token size that's about 20M tokens/day. does that math match yours?
[04:28] Lina: mm that seems right, 100k * 200 = 20M, yes.

[05:40] Alex: budget wise, what's a hard cap and what's flexible?
[05:44] James: we have a monthly budget cap for this POC of $12k. it's a firm limit for the trial.
[05:51] Priya: ok that's helpful — we'll run scenarios: hosted on Redwood with our standard model (we'll suggest a 7B-13B open model variant) vs dedicated reserved capacity with quantization.

[07:10] Priya: quick note on latency SLOs — what are your p50/p95 targets?
[07:16] Lina: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 300ms ideally. For user-facing flows we care about p95 more.
[07:23] Priya: ok, those are achievable with the right config but it's a tradeoff with batching. batching improves cost but adds latency variance.

[08:05] Evan: on infra side, we need to know if you require VPC peering or private deployment for the POC. For security, we prefer traffic over our VPC.
[08:14] Alex: for the POC we can run against hosted but with VPC egress allowed, or we can do a Dedicated trial. Hosted is faster to start; Dedicated takes lead time for reserved GPU allocation.
[08:29] James: how long for Dedicated to be available?
[08:31] Priya: typically 2–3 weeks to schedule a dedicated pool for a POC depending on region. so for timeline, hosted benchmark first is faster.

[10:02] Priya: showing rough per-token estimates — these are ballpark: hosted (unquantized) about $0.00012 per input token and $0.00018 per output token for 13B open model on our hosted tier; end-to-end that's ~ $0.0003 per request with 200 tokens => $0.06 per request, so at 100k requests/day that's $6k/day which obviously exceeds your budget, so we need to rely on batching and caching, or use smaller model/quantized variant.
[10:36] James: that sounds high. can you break down where most cost is coming from?
[10:40] Priya: majority is GPU time — generation cost scales with output tokens and model size. batching reduces per-token compute by increasing GPU utilization; caching eliminates prefix work for repeated context. also routing non-critical traffic to cheaper model variants can reduce unit cost by 2–4x.

[12:00] Priya: example scenarios:
- Scenario A: Hosted, no batching, default model: expected monthly spend ~ $180k (not possible).
- Scenario B: Hosted with batching and KV cache hits ~30%, and a smaller 7B quantized variant for partial traffic: monthly ~ $9k–$12k (close to your POC cap).
- Scenario C: Dedicated quantized pool (int8) with autoscale for bursts: unit cost lower, estimated monthly ~ $5k–$8k but with setup/commit requirements.

[13:12] James: are those quantization numbers validated? we care about quality impact.
[13:18] Priya: yes, we run model-specific evals. quantization to int8 typically adds small quality delta for many tasks; we'll run your eval set as part of the POC.

[15:00] Priya: about batching — we can do dynamic batching with latency caps. e.g., set a 40ms batching window to gather small groups which maintains p50 but helps p95 somewhat; larger windows increase throughput efficiency but add tail latency.
[15:20] Lina: we're worried about p95 — can we set conditional batching only for non-interactive flows?
[15:26] Priya: yes, you can route interactive flows to low-latency path (no batching) and background jobs to batched endpoints. that's a common pattern.

[17:10] Evan: caching: what do you mean by KV cache? we have some prefix reuse in our app.
[17:16] Priya: KV cache (we sometimes see it transcribed as KV cash) stores decoder state for prefixes so repeated context doesn't recompute. for instruction-following with repeating system prompts, we often get 20–40% reduction in compute. depends on prompt reuse.

[19:05] James: ok we can run an analysis on prompt reuse. I'll share logs.

[20:00] Priya: on benchmarking, plan: you give us 200–500 sample prompts covering interactive and bulk flows, we'll run hosted benchmarks to capture p50/p95, throughput, and cost per token. we'll also run a quantized dedicated run if you want to explore that.
[20:20] Alex: timeline wise — if we get prompts and traffic profile by end of this week (12/3), Redwood can do hosted benchmark in the week of 12/7 and share results by 12/09. then we sync and pick the POC path. Does that align?
[20:34] James: yes that's tight but doable.

[22:40] Priya: security checklist — you mentioned SOC2 and SSO?
[22:44] Lina: yes SOC2 Type II required, SAML SSO integration, KMS for encryption at rest, audit logs, and data residency for EU when we scale.
[22:55] Alex: Redwood supports SOC2, SAML, KMS, and can provide an audit pack. for EU residency we have region options. we'll include links to our security pack.

[25:10] James: any contract/commitment for Dedicated?
[25:14] Alex: Dedicated tends to have monthly reserved capacity commitments; for POC we can do a short-term reserved trial or use flexible burst credits. we'll outline options in the POC proposal.

[27:00] Priya: benchmarks we care about capturing: tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, throughput at target concurrency, token utilization (wasted compute), and quality metrics (ROUGE/F1 or human evals you prefer).
[27:18] Lina: we'll provide the evaluation script and preferred quality thresholds.

[29:30] James: what about rate limits and throttling in hosted? we have large bursts.
[29:36] Alex: we can configure per-route quotas and burst capacity; also can route excess traffic to lower-cost model or queue with backpressure.

[31:10] Priya: cost sensitivity — to hit your $12k POC cap, modeling shows we need a mix: 35–50% of traffic to be served by a quantized 7B variant or cached responses, and batching to achieve effective token discounts. otherwise hosted default models will blow past the cap.

[33:20] Evan: curious on how you estimate quantized perf improvements in latency.
[33:25] Priya: quantized models reduce memory bandwidth and can lower latency slightly on some kernels, but biggest win is lower GPU memory enabling smaller instances and higher density, which reduces $/token. We'll validate in the dedicated run.

[36:05] James: any suggestions for prioritizing which flows to route to cheap model?
[36:10] Priya: yes: non-critical internal summaries, batch analytics, and low-risk autofill can go to cheaper models. interactive chat should stay on higher-quality path.

[38:15] Alex: for the cost spreadsheet we'll include scenario toggles: model size, quantization, batch window, cache hit rate, and expected monthly spend. you'll be able to change inputs.

[40:00] Lina: do you support customer-managed keys for encryption?
[40:03] Alex: yes, we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private/Dedicated and also for hosted via bring-your-own-key options.

[42:22] James: ok so next steps recap?
[42:26] Alex: 1) Sierra sends representative prompts and traffic profile by 12/03. 2) Redwood sends cost model spreadsheet by 12/03. 3) Redwood runs hosted benchmark week of 12/7 and shares results by 12/09. 4) Follow-up sync to decide POC path week of 12/10.
[42:45] James: yep we'll do that.

[45:00] Priya: any other blockers?
[45:05] Evan: network/firewall rules — we'll need IP allowlist for the hosted runner.
[45:10] Alex: noted, we'll provide IP ranges and also can run via a peered VPC for the Dedicated option.

[48:00] James: big picture, if the numbers look good we want to expand to 1M queries/day in Q1.
[48:06] Priya: great — we'll include scale estimates.

[51:00] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and security pack.
[51:06] Lina: thanks all.
[51:08] James: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
